in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

To assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your situation. According to the rules, you can still qualify for Child Benefit even if your child doesn't live with you, as long as you're contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep (covering things like food, clothes, pocket money, or financial contributions for their accommodation).

I can see you mentioned a weekly upkeep contribution of £10.00 for Alex. To determine eligibility, I need to compare this to the current Child Benefit rate:

**Current Child Benefit rates are:**
- **£25.60 per week** for the eldest or only child
- £16.95 per week for each additional child

Since Alex appears to be your only child in this claim, you would need to be contributing at least **£25.60 per week** (or the equivalent amount monthly/as a lump sum for a set period) to continue receiving Child Benefit while Alex lives with someone else.

Based on your situation:
- You contribute £10.00 per week for Alex's upkeep
- The minimum required contribution is £25.60 per week

Unfortunately, this means your contribution is below the threshold needed to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond the initial 8-week period after Alex went to live with someone else.

Let me provide my formal assessment:

**Summary:** I'm sorry, but you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

While you could receive Child Benefit for the first 8 weeks after Alex went to live with someone else (assuming no one else has claimed), to continue receiving it beyond that period, you would need to contribute at least £25.60 per week towards Alex's upkeep. Your current contribution of £10.00 per week falls short of this requirement.

**Options to consider:**
- If you're able to increase your contributions to at least £25.60 per week (covering things like clothes, food, pocket money, or financial help with accommodation), you could contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your eligibility
- The person Alex currently lives with may be eligible to claim Child Benefit if they're responsible for Alex's day-to-day care

If you have any questions or if your circumstances change, please feel free to ask!
